Legacy radish S3 methods

Source: R/radish_optimize.R
legacy_radish_methods.Rd

Deprecated S3 methods retained for legacy objects that still dispatch on the older "radish" class names.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'radish'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'radish'
summary(object, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.radish'
print(
  x,
  digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L),
  signif.stars = getOption("show.signif.stars"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'radish'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'radish'
fitted(object, type = c("response", "distance", "covariance"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'radish'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, method = "permutation", ...)

# S3 method for class 'radish'
anova(object, ..., alternative = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'radish'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'radish'
AIC(object, ..., k = 2)

# S3 method for class 'radish'
residuals(object, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted legacy radish object.

digits

Number of digits to print.

...

Additional arguments passed through to generic methods.

object, alternative

Fitted legacy radish objects.

conf.level

Confidence level for nuisance-parameter confidence intervals reported by summary(). These intervals are conditional on the fitted conductance surface.

signif.stars

Should significance stars be printed in coefficient tables?

type

Type of fitted values to return.

nsim

Number of simulated response matrices to generate.

seed

Optional random seed used by simulate().

method

Simulation method.

k

Penalty multiplier supplied to AIC().

Value

  • print() returns its input invisibly after printing it.

  • summary() returns a list of class summary.terradish and summary.radish, containing conductance and nuisance-parameter estimates, uncertainty tables, convergence diagnostics, log-likelihood, and model-comparison statistics. Conductance coefficients are on the log-conductance scale; nuisance-parameter uncertainty is conditional on the fitted conductance surface.

  • coef() returns a named numeric vector of fitted conductance coefficients, or an empty vector when they are unidentified.

  • fitted() returns a numeric focal-site matrix of expected responses, resistance distances, or graph covariances, selected by type.

  • simulate() returns a numeric response matrix for nsim = 1, or a three-dimensional array with simulations along the third dimension otherwise.

  • anova() returns a matrix of class anova, comparing two nested fits by log-likelihood, parameter count, likelihood-ratio statistic, and its reference-distribution p-value.

  • logLik() returns a numeric scalar of class logLik, with parameter-count and focal-site-count attributes.

  • AIC() returns a numeric scalar equal to \(-2\ell + kK\), where \(K\) is the number of estimated parameters. Smaller values favor a fit when response and likelihood are comparable.

  • residuals() returns a numeric matrix of observed minus fitted responses, centered for covariance-response models.

See terradish_methods for interpretation and comparison requirements.
